signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Policy Divergence
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 107.27, pressured by an acute weekly divergence across G10 peers where JPY leads with a 1W average of +0.856% across 7 pairs while AUD lags at -0.930% across 4 pairs, creating a 1.786% bilateral spread. BoJ holds at 1.25%. AONIA at 4.85% vs TONA at 1.23% preserves a 362bp carry advantage for AUD, yet spot remains deeply depressed and screens cheap against fair value models at z=-2.47σ. The pair trades against severe downtrend momentum in the broader AUD complex, with AUD/USD sitting extended below its SMA20 at 0.6951 and SMA50 at 0.7004. Risk-off sentiment characterized by VIX at 22.9 accelerates carry liquidation despite hawkish RBA meeting minutes. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY, momentum and safe-haven demand overriding the carry advantage. Catalyst: Australia Wage Price Index and Employment Change 18 Nov. Risk: Broad equity rebound compresses the 1.786% G10 spread and triggers an unwind back toward the model fair value of 110.15.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Technical Resistance
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.33, holding below the critical 160.00 psychological threshold that capped rallies across multiple sessions. Saxo Bank 1M 25-delta risk reversals print at -1.74, reflecting an extreme put skew as institutional desks aggressively hedge downside exposure ahead of 160.00 verbal intervention risks. Leveraged funds hold net short positioning of -23,913 contracts (90th percentile, z=+1.33), leaving the market exposed to long unwinds if intervention warnings accelerate. The spot rate sits above its SMA20 at 158.27 and SMA50 at 157.52, while 1M implied volatility at 7.2% trades at a 1.9-point premium over 30-day realized volatility of 5.4%. A 267bp OIS spread favoring USD (SOFR 3.90% vs TONA 1.23%) keeps baseline carry intact, but topside participation remains constrained by bilateral macro event risk. Trade bias: Neutral/short USD/JPY, capped by 160.00 resistance and aggressive options put skew. Catalyst: FOMC Minutes release 19:00 UTC. Risk: A confirmed break and daily close above 160.00 without official intervention triggers short-covering toward multi-decade highs.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Real Yield Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0999, breaking below the 1.10 handle to mark fresh multi-month lows while positioned well below its SMA20 of 1.1164 and SMA50 of 1.1285. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short -98,604 contracts, sitting in the 6th percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.58, indicating positioning saturation. Rates markets reflect persistent USD dominance, supported by an SOFR-€STR carry differential of +146bp (SOFR 3.90% vs €STR 2.44%) alongside Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65%. US 5-year yields advanced 26bp over the past 5 sessions, led entirely by a 25bp surge in real yields to 2.64% alongside just 1bp of breakeven expansion (FRED, as of Nov 12). Concurrently, retail positioning at Retail sentiment data shows 87% long exposure, creating an acute institutional-versus-retail divergence that risks further liquidation if spot fails to hold key psychological support. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, driven by real yield expansion and structural carry divergence. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI report 18 Nov. Risk: Leveraged funds covering crowded shorts after EUR/USD reclaims the SMA20 at 1.1164.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Labor Data Resilience Ahead of CPI
signals.text: GBP/USD prints at 1.3188, trading below its SMA20 of 1.3355 and SMA50 of 1.3334 in an established short-term downtrend. UK labor data released this morning showed solid domestic resilience, with employment change surging by 156k against the 25k forecast and unemployment falling to 4.6% vs 4.7% expected. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold a net long position of +35,586 contracts (71st percentile, z=+0.55), reflecting solid speculative backing for Bank of England policy tightening. The OIS spread sits at -8bp (SOFR 3.90% vs SONIA 3.98%), leaving the carry picture balanced between both currencies while the BoE benchmark at 4.00% matches the Fed policy rate at 4.00%. Volatility remains contained, with GBP/USD 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.2% against realized volatility of 5.5%, displaying a mild 0.7-point volatility risk premium. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, technical downward momentum counterbalanced by labor market strength. Catalyst: UK CPI release 18 Nov. Risk: A downside miss in headline UK inflation undermines December BoE rate hike pricing and breaks support below 1.3100.
